claims.text: Conventional elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding exhibit Cr–Zr interdiffusion at elevated temperatures.
An ultrathin Al2O3 interlayer can reduce Cr–Zr interdiffusion at high temperatures.
Reducing Cr–Zr interdiffusion with an Al2O3 interlayer will improve Cr-coating durability in both subcritical water and high-temperature steam.
Protective coatings, including metallic Cr coatings, are used on zirconium-alloy cladding to improve high-temperature oxidation resistance.
PWR primary-water corrosion resistance is important during normal reactor operation.
High-temperature steam oxidation is a critical concern for accident-tolerant zirconium-alloy cladding during a LOCA.
An ultrathin, conformal Al2O3 layer can be deposited directly on zirconium alloy before application of elemental Cr.
The ultrathin Al2O3 layer acts as a stable high-temperature diffusion barrier at the Zr-alloy/Cr interface.
The Al2O3 interlayer inhibits atomic migration between Cr and Zr.
Alumina is chemically inert under the proposed service environments.
Alumina maintains its structure under both moderate reactor temperatures and extreme accident temperatures.
Interfacial Cr–Zr atom exchange causes premature failure of elemental Cr coatings.
The Al2O3 barrier will suppress Cr–Zr atom exchange without compromising the oxidation resistance supplied by the Cr coating.
Relative to a directly applied Cr coating, the Al2O3-interlayer coating will significantly reduce interfacial Cr and Zr transport.
Relative to a directly applied Cr coating, the Al2O3-interlayer coating will better maintain coating integrity during normal PWR operation.
Relative to a directly applied Cr coating, the Al2O3-interlayer coating will better maintain coating integrity during high-temperature steam accident exposure.
The long-term stability of the Al2O3 interlayer under cyclic thermal and irradiation conditions is unresolved and requires experimental validation.
